d4fd6c272bc5: Every other Tuesday. The 2nd and 4th Friday. The last Saturday of the month. These are ordinary business rules, and Salesforce has no field that expresses any of them.
e26c4ef3305e: Recurrence exists in Salesforce for Events and Tasks, and it stops there. The moment your schedule lives on a custom object (a shift, a session, an inspection, an on-call rotation), you are on your own, and the usual answer is that somebody works the dates out on a paper calendar and enters them by hand.
dd57641a12d9: The two kinds of recurrence people mean
960efc5bf518: They get conflated, and they need different logic.
aec9ca026e50: Every week, every 2 weeks, every 3 weeks
912215ce7aa0: A day of week plus a repeat interval
681509b9ad57: Interval recurrence counts forward from a start date and does not care about month boundaries. Occurrence recurrence resets every month, and "last" is awkward because it lands on the 4th or 5th week depending on the month. That single word is where most hand-rolled implementations break.
5402ee45ca41: Why writing it yourself goes wrong
535ed2199482: "The 5th Monday" exists in some months and not others.
1c2456561a65: They quietly shift every calculation that assumes a fixed year.
88f066c7b188: Every other week starting when? Two people will disagree.
62a3e2bf5b7a: They may need skipping, and your holidays live in your own org data.
accb14d98d6a: It creates thousands of records nobody asked for.
10e18fc95da9: None of these are hard individually. Together they are a week of work and a permanent source of edge-case bugs.
ba7fadb26027: Generating dates instead of storing a rule
9ade16d13493: There is a design decision underneath the algorithm: do you store the <t1>rule</t1> and expand it at read time, or expand it once and store the resulting <t2>dates</t2>?
3fb9bdd898a1: Storing dates is almost always the better answer in Salesforce. Concrete date records report, roll up, filter, and drive automation like any other data. A stored rule needs interpreting everywhere it is used, and Salesforce reporting cannot interpret it at all. The tradeoff is that changing the pattern means regenerating, which is why the pattern picker belongs at the point of entry rather than buried in configuration.
17c6c577ff7a: Custom Day-of-Week comes first, because no standard field expresses it at all. Pick any combination of weekdays, set the interval, give it a range, and the calendar fills in every matching date before you save anything.

d07b3bc437e8: Weekdays and Weekends are the two shortcuts people reach for most, and they do the same expansion with one click.
6104021505e8: Weekdays: every Monday through Friday in the range.
1c7638f75d82: Weekends: every Saturday and Sunday, for coverage and on-call.
096dab5751c1: Let people see the dates before they commit
c5d8ec69f78f: The best thing a recurrence UI can do is show its work. When the user picks "every 2 weeks on Tuesday" and immediately sees the actual dates highlighted on a calendar, mistakes get caught in the second before saving rather than the week after. It also settles the "every other week starting when" argument instantly, because the anchor is visible.
ad3ab9248b1b: The same applies to consolidation. If your recurring selection produces Monday to Friday for six weeks, you may want thirty records or you may want six, one per week, with a start and end date. Deciding that at selection time is far cheaper than migrating afterwards.
